text: `SiteFooter` HIDES ITS SCREEN-READER TEXT WITH ITS OWN CLASS, SO IT RENDERS CORRECTLY OUTSIDE THE HUB. It used Tailwind's `sr-only`, which the design system never declares — so it worked only where a consumer happened to load Tailwind. In Storybook the "Site footer" heading, every "(opens in a new window)" note and all five social labels rendered on screen, the labels piled over the chips. It now uses `.ds-sr-only`, declared in `site-footer.css` as every other component that needs it does. The handoff audit that found it also corrected what Dev Mode, the docs and Storybook say about the component: the Code Connect template named Tier-1 palette primitives the architecture forbids components to consume; the docs page, the snippet and Storybook linked Help to `/website/help`, which is not a route; the docs page claimed ten brand modes where there are eight; Storybook listed `columns` as required and omitted `sitemap` and `help`, drew both credit marks as placeholder images from an outside service, and quoted the retired lineage sentence; and `design.md` contradicted itself on parity and ran to 1,667 words, now 760 with every rule kept
